key_insight: Query-agnostic compression can reduce multi-vector document representations to a constant, small set of vectors per document while preserving late-interaction retrieval quality across modalities (text, images, video, audio).
problem_solved: Late-interaction retrieval's compute and storage costs scale linearly with document length (or number of region/segment vectors), making it expensive for image-, video-, and audio-rich corpora; this paper tackles compressing multi-vector document encodings under a fixed vector budget.
method: Compress variable-length multi-vector document representations into a constant number of vectors per document using query-agnostic strategies.

Employ compact representations (e.g., learned codebooks / clustering, residual quantization or centroid substitution) and index-level mapping to preserve late-interaction signal while reducing storage and computation.
Design a modality-agnostic pipeline that integrates compressed multi-vector documents into retrieval indices so late interaction can be computed more efficiently at query time.
impact: Enables practical late-interaction retrieval for large, multimodal corpora by cutting index size and query computation without needing query-specific reprocessing — letting practitioners deploy high-accuracy retrieval on image/video/audio-heavy datasets at much lower cost.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram: document with many region vectors → same document represented by a few compressed vectors (constant budget).
Flowchart: encoding → compression (codebook/clustering) → index storage → late-interaction scoring at query time.
Bar chart: relative storage and compute (raw multi-vector vs. compressed index) with retrieval accuracy preserved.
Modal comparison icons: text, image, video, audio with arrows showing same compression pipeline applied to each modality.
paper_title: Multi-Vector Index Compression in Any Modality
paper_authors: Hanxiang Qin, Alexander Martin, Rohan Jha, Chunsheng Zuo, Reno Kriz
